title: Tait-case driver pleads guilty
article: The driver of the stolen vehicle in which 16-year-old Kyle Tait was shot to death last August by a New Westminster police officer pleaded guilty yesterday to a number of criminal charges stemming from the incident.

Ian James Campbell, 18, pleaded guilty to dangerous driving, a flight-related charge, possession of stolen property and two counts of assault with a weapon. He did not enter a plea on the most serious charge, criminal negligence causing death. The prosecution is likely to stay that charge after he is sentenced for the other offences.
Mr. Campbell has been in custody since the incident. His lawyer, Paul Del Rossi, said yesterday it would be inappropriate to comment before a sentencing hearing takes place May 11.

An RCMP-led probe is continuing into the conduct of New Westminster Constable Todd Sweet, who fired the shot that killed Mr. Tait. The teen and three other youths were passengers in the sport-utility vehicle Mr. Campbell was driving. Everyone in the car was unarmed, according to a wrongful-death lawsuit Mr. Tait's family filed in February.

When Mr. Campbell was charged last October, New Westminster police said he had been trying to ram a police car and that the lives of Constable Sweet and his partner were in danger when three shots were fired into the SUV.
The wrongful-death lawsuit alleges the officer approached the SUV in an "agitated and enraged state" and fired three shots "indiscriminately" into the vehicle.
Constable Sweet is facing two other unrelated lawsuits alleging excessive force. None of the allegations has been proved in court.

A lawsuit filed by a Port Coquitlam labourer who said Constable Sweet and a colleague assaulted him was settled out of court in 2004. The terms were not made public and there was no admission of wrongdoing.
Constable Sweet is on an undisclosed "operational assignment," according to court documents filed by the New Westminster Police Service.
